A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same M-AUPO research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching material across appendix renumbering.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendix I report original synthetic experiments and evaluations on TREC-DL and NECTAR, including performance curves, runtimes, and selected assortment sizes.

after.justification: Section 6 and Appendix H report original synthetic and real-data evaluations, with revised performance results, separate PL/RB runtimes, and assortment-size measurements.

M1.justification: Section 4 replaces v1's reference-action objective based on average feature-distance norms with separate probability-weighted, squared, mean-centered uncertainty objectives for PL and RB. Selection now starts from the best pair and greedily adds actions with nonnegative marginal gain. The OMD losses and updates largely remain, but the central exploration procedure changes substantially. Appendix G.1 also introduces an assortment rule for cumulative-regret minimization.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same four synthetic scenarios: stochastic, non-contextual, hard-to-learn, and skewed contexts, alongside TREC-DL and NECTAR. The new regret-minimization extension is theoretical and introduces no evaluated dataset or task.

E2.justification: DopeWolfe, Uniform, and Best&Ref participate in the corresponding comparisons in both versions, with the same described baseline adaptations. Although v1's main figure captions mention only DopeWolfe, their legends and plotted results already include all three baselines; v3's broader captions do not add comparators.

E3.justification: Sections 6.2 and I.2/H.2 change the reported real-data configuration from PL-only to RB-only. The revised synthetic PL selection uses five Monte Carlo samples to approximate its ranking expectation. Dataset sizes, feature dimensions, evaluation intervals, and the realized-regret proxy remain unchanged. Figure 2 retains a PL label, so the protocol revision does not establish that every displayed experiment was rerun.

E4.justification: The existing K sweeps, PL/RB performance comparisons, and four synthetic stress scenarios are retained. Table H.1 extends the computational analysis by reporting separate PL and RB runtimes, whereas Table I.1 provided one M-AUPO runtime column. This adds a targeted comparison of the two variants' computational costs.

E5.justification: Both versions report 20 independent synthetic runs and 10 independent real-data runs, with different random seeds and standard errors. No new empirical confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures are documented.

E6.justification: The revision changes central performance results and the reported PL/RB relationship. In Figure 1, the K=5 PL M-AUPO bar changes from 0.02 to 0.04, while the RB bar remains 0.02. Runtime and assortment-size results also change: at K=5, Table I.1 reports 2.94 seconds for M-AUPO, while Table H.1 reports 2.71 seconds for PL and 1.10 seconds for RB. These are revised results for a changed selection procedure, not demonstrated same-method performance gains.

T1.justification: The upper-bound proofs replace the reference-based covariance comparison with expected-Hessian and weighted-uncertainty arguments. Theorem 1's remainder changes from d^2 K^2 e^(4B)/T to d^2 K^4 e^(6B)/T, with an added horizon condition. The RB confidence analysis explicitly addresses dependent comparisons and adds a small-K restriction. V1's arbitrary-reference and feature-diversity results are removed; v3 adds a cumulative-regret theorem and restricts the stated active-learning extension to RB. The lower-bound theorem and its proof are essentially retained.

C1.justification: The central claims about larger assortments improving sample efficiency and avoiding exponential parameter dependence in the leading term remain. V3 adds computational and empirical superiority of RB over PL as an explicit introduction contribution and recasts the claimed analytical contribution around the warm-up/non-warm-up decomposition.

C2.justification: V3 replaces the interpretation that PL and RB perform nearly identically with an explanation favoring RB because it avoids ranking-expectation approximation. It adds discussion of the small-K applicability restriction and removes the diversity-based explanation for Uniform. Section 5.2 also replaces v1's acknowledged upper/lower-bound gap with a claim that the bounds match when assortment size equals K, although the displayed bounds still differ by a factor of sqrt(K).

D1.justification: Appendix H.1 newly specifies five Monte Carlo samples for the revised PL expectation calculation, and Section 4 explains the corresponding approximation cost and separate PL/RB selection complexities. Hardware, feature extraction and normalization, baseline sampling budgets, and dataset/model access information are substantially retained.

R1.justification: The core positioning against Zhu, Mukherjee, and Thekumparampil remains. V3 adds Ville's work for the new martingale argument and removes references including Kim et al., Lattimore and Szepesvari, Stiennon et al., and Tropp alongside discarded analyses. Other title and publication updates concern retained works rather than new literature coverage.

P1.justification: Section 4 and the main proof sketch are substantially rewritten, with separate PL/RB selection explanations and a reorganized analytical narrative. The conclusion is condensed, the standalone efficient-assortment appendix disappears, and the additional-discussion appendix is substantially restructured. These are extensive changes to existing explanations and organization beyond simple renumbering.

P2.justification: The two main figures and five appendix experiment figures retain their general panel structures. Presentation changes include corrected baseline captions, separate PL/RB columns in the runtime table, removal of Procedure A.1, and redistribution of appendix figures and tables. The final assortment-size table moves onto an otherwise nearly empty page.

improvement.justification: V3 improves transparency by discussing dependence between rank-broken comparisons, stating additional theorem restrictions, and separating PL/RB implementation costs. However, it introduces an unsupported exact-matching interpretation of the lower bound and reports RB-only real-data experiments while Figure 2 still identifies PL. These inconsistencies affect the central theoretical and empirical evidence. The substantial analytical revision and added detail therefore coexist with losses in internal consistency, leaving the net quality direction uncertain.
